chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.meaning: What changed: the dollar slipped off its 18-month highs overnight after Trump ruled out new Iran strikes before the November 3 midterms — DXY eased to about 102.1, down roughly 0.1%. The move is about the war premium leaking out, not the Fed: the 10-year actually fell 4.9bp to 5.232% after a strong $22B 30-year auction stopped at 5.618%, the highest since 2000. Thread: the hawkish-hold thesis is in its third week — FOMC minutes had 'most' officials seeing another hike by year-end, December is around 83% priced, and jobless claims came in at 197k, the fourth straight week near 57-year lows, keeping the labor floor intact. What it means: this confirms the prior thesis. The hawkish chorus all spoke Thursday — Waller said more hikes are probably needed (flexible on timing), Musalem said rates may need to climb for 6–9 more months, Kashkari penciled in one more this year and another in 2027. The Iran de-escalation shaves the war premium, not the rate repricing: the dollar is softer on risk, not on the Fed.
chapters.fx: What to watch: U Mich sentiment 9am CT (consensus 47.5; the 5–10y inflation expectations, last 3.4%, matter more than the headline) and Collins at 3pm CT. Then the swing event: CPI Wed Oct 14, 7:30am CT — core m/m of 0.2% or below validates disinflation; 0.3%+ revives October (currently ~17–19%).

scenarios.base: Fed holds its hawkish tone into the Oct 27–28 FOMC; USD stays bid while Dec hike odds hold near 80%+.
scenarios.bear: Soft CPI or a dovish FOMC surprise collapses hike odds; crowded USD longs unwind.
scenarios.bull: Oct 14 CPI beats expectations — Dec gets fully priced and DXY extends to fresh highs.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.meaning: What changed: EUR/USD steadied around 1.1211, off Monday's 17-month low of 1.1161, as the French selloff stabilized — the French 10-year briefly topped 5% for the first time since July 2002 before Le Pen's €25B-a-year spending-cut plan pulled yields down about 11bp. The OAT–Bund spread sits near 140–146bp, off the >150bp wides (widest since 2011–12). Thread: the euro has fallen four straight weeks, with French fiscal stress layering a sovereign risk premium onto the ECB-policy drag. What it means: this breaks the relief-bounce hope from yesterday's edition. ECB chief economist Lane added a dovish tint — higher borrowing costs could curb demand and reduce the need for further tightening — even as markets price roughly 80% odds of another ECB hike by year-end. Spain's snap election (Sánchez called it after housing measures were rejected) adds political noise. The fiscal risk premium is off the wides, but it is not gone.
chapters.fx: What to watch: French budget bills hit the National Assembly plenary Oct 13, key votes late Nov–mid Dec, and an Aa3 rating review this month. On the chart, 1.1161 is the line: a break risks 1.1065; a hold plus fading fiscal fear opens a relief bounce toward 1.13.

scenarios.base: EUR/USD pinned near 1.12; French fiscal headlines keep a risk premium on EUR.
scenarios.bull: 1.1161 holds, budget process calms spreads — relief toward 1.13.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.meaning: What changed: GBP/USD firmed to about 1.3228 on the softer dollar, and sterling sits at a 16-month high against the euro (EUR/GBP 84.74p) as French contagion fears push money toward London. Thread: the BoE held Bank Rate at 3.75% in a 6–3 vote — three members wanted another hike. UK CPI was 3.1% in August and the Bank sees around 3.75% in Q4, slightly above 4% early next year. The BoE also paused gilt sales for six months and halted long-dated sales — a fiscal-stress valve. What it means: confirms the hawkish-hold thesis. Inflation is still the story in Britain, and the Bank is leaning against it even as gilt markets wobble. The pound is the relative winner of Europe's fiscal stress so far — bid vs the euro, riding the dollar's softness.
chapters.fx: What to watch: September CPI (consensus ~3.5% — release date unconfirmed, not stated here); Chancellor Healey's first Budget on Oct 28; S&P's UK rating review today; BoE decision Nov 5.

scenarios.base: GBP consolidates the 1.32 area; hawkish-hold keeps a floor under it.
scenarios.bear: Dovish BoE or fiscal wobble — GBP gives back the euro-driven gains.
scenarios.bull: Hot UK CPI revives hike bets — GBP/USD pushes higher.

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.meaning: What changed: USD/JPY held around 158.05 — steady, and the only G10 pair where the dollar actually gained overnight (about 0.1%). BoJ branch managers said cost-push price pressure is broadening into consumer businesses; Governor Ueda flagged that underlying inflation could overshoot 2% and signaled continued tightening intent; OIS now prices a December hike above 80%. Thread: the US–Japan rate gap has owned this pair — a 24-year-high US 10-year against a BoJ still at 1.25%. Japan's August current-account surplus beat (¥4.062T), and PM Takaichi is pushing food-consumption-tax cuts funded without new bonds. What it means: confirms the hiking-cycle thesis — the Oct 29–30 BoJ meeting is live. The tension is pure: the haven bid softens as Iran fears ease, but the wide yield gap caps any yen rally. Intervention watch stays on if USD/JPY pushes toward 160.
chapters.fx: What to watch: BoJ Oct 29–30; any US CPI surprise that moves the US 10Y moves this pair first.

scenarios.base: Rate gap dominates; USD/JPY consolidates below the 159–160 resistance zone.
scenarios.bear: US yields push higher — USD/JPY tests 160 and intervention talk returns.
scenarios.bull: Risk-off escalation or dovish Fed repricing — JPY rallies, USD/JPY breaks lower.

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.meaning: What changed: USD/CHF traded around 0.832 — the franc gained about 0.2% overnight on safe-haven demand, but the haven bid is softening as Trump de-escalates. EUR/CHF held near 0.9324. Thread: the franc was the haven of choice this week — Iran/Hormuz escalation plus French bond stress both bid it. What it means: mildly breaks the escalating-haven-bid thesis — the fear trade is leaking out of CHF as the strike headlines fade. With the SNB pinned at 0.00% (next decision Dec 10), the franc remains a pure geopolitical play, not a rates story.
chapters.fx: What to watch: any Iran/Saudi headlines overnight; if Tehran confirms the talks track, expect further haven unwind (CHF softer).

scenarios.base: CHF drifts as the haven bid unwinds gradually; USD/CHF holds the low-0.83s.
scenarios.bear: Confirmed Hormuz reopening — CHF gives back the week's gains.
scenarios.bull: Fresh escalation — haven flows flood back into CHF.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.meaning: What changed: AUD/USD rose to about 0.70 (+0.26%) — the best G10 performer as the dollar softened and yields eased. The RBA sits on hold at 4.60% with a hawkish stance, and China reopened after Golden Week ended Oct 7. Thread: the Aussie has been squeezed between a hiking RBA and risk-off flows — the risk proxy with the best policy tailwind in G10. What it means: confirms the de-escalation relief thesis for risk proxies — oil still above $103 keeps the commodity bid, and a softer dollar does the rest. AUD/JPY near 110.6 stays capped by the US–Japan rate gap spilling into yen crosses.
chapters.fx: What to watch: China CPI Wed Oct 14; RBA next meets Nov 2–3 (was the Sep 29 hike one-and-done?); any Iran headlines flip risk sentiment fast.

scenarios.base: AUD firms with risk sentiment; 0.70 holds while de-escalation lasts.
scenarios.bear: Re-escalation or hot US CPI — AUD/NZD give back the relief rally first.
scenarios.bull: Confirmed Hormuz reopening + soft US CPI — risk-on, AUD extends.

chapters.teaser: Aussie the best G10 performer as the dollar softens — de-escalation relief meets a hawkish RBA on hold at 4.60%.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.meaning: What changed: USD/CAD slipped to about 1.42 (−0.4%) as the loonie drew support from Brent holding above $103. Canada's September jobs report lands today at 7:30am CT (consensus +6.1K, unemployment 6.5% vs 6.4%, after −41.7K). Thread: CAD has been the terms-of-trade winner of the oil spike; the BoC sits neutral at 2.25% with its Oct 28 decision and MPR next. The supply-shock premium is intact despite de-escalation: Hormuz crude crossings are down 27% to 10.1 mbd (a two-month low), and Hurricane Isaias shut 62.9% of Gulf of Mexico output (about 1.3 mbd). What it means: confirms the oil-bid thesis — the physical market is still tight even as the fear premium leaks. A soft jobs print would reinforce the BoC's neutral-to-dovish lean; a beat with $103 oil complicates it.
chapters.fx: What to watch: Canada jobs 7:30am CT today; BoC decision + MPR Oct 28 (13:45 UTC).

scenarios.base: CAD stays supported while Brent holds above ~$100; USD/CAD drifts lower on oil.
scenarios.bear: Jobs miss + de-escalation unwinds the oil premium — USD/CAD bounces.
scenarios.bull: Jobs beat + oil firm — CAD extends gains into the BoC.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.meaning: What changed: NZD/USD firmed to about 0.5615 (+0.2%) on the softer dollar and easing yields. Westpac now expects the RBNZ to pause on Oct 28 and hike 25bp in December instead (OCR 2.75%), plus two more in early 2027. Thread: the RBNZ hiked to 2.75% on Sep 2 as fuel inflation ran hot; the market had around 75% priced for another hike in October. What it means: breaks the 'October hike likely' lean — if the RBNZ pauses, the hawkish repricing unwinds and NZD softens. The pause call rests on an uneven recovery, not on inflation being beaten.
chapters.fx: What to watch: RBNZ decision Oct 28 (01:00 UTC) — pause vs hike is now a genuine two-way bet; dairy prices and oil as the swing factors.

scenarios.base: NZD drifts with risk sentiment; RBNZ pause priced in gradually.
scenarios.bear: RBNZ pauses and sounds done — NZD underperforms the commodity bloc.
scenarios.bull: RBNZ hikes Oct 28 after all — NZD re-rates higher.

chapters.teaser: Kiwi firms on the softer dollar, but Westpac's RBNZ pause call breaks the October-hike lean.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Brent ~$102.80, WTI ~$90.70 — and the $12+ spread between them is the story: the war premium sits in seaborne crude, not US landlocked oil.
chapters.meaning: What changed: crude gave back more today — Brent down 1.4% to ~$102.80, WTI off 1% to ~$90.70 — as Trump's no-strikes pledge kept the market defensive and Hurricane Isaias shut in some Gulf production without lifting prices. Thread: oil has been the swing factor for CAD all week — every escalation headline lifted it, every de-escalation headline pressed it back down. What it means: the number that matters isn't either price, it's the $12.40 gap between them — roughly triple the normal spread. That wide gap is the geopolitical premium made visible: it lives in Brent, the seaborne benchmark exposed to Hormuz, while WTI, landlocked in Oklahoma, barely feels it. For FX this is a terms-of-trade transfer with an asterisk. Canada's crude prices off WTI, so the loonie feels the softer ~$90.70 print more than the Brent headline — a headwind arriving just as the +60.4K jobs beat was building a hawkish BoC case. Japan and the eurozone, pricing imports off Brent, get relief either way: cheaper energy eases import bills, a quiet positive for JPY and EUR.
numbers: Goldman: Sept risk premium ~$22/bbl on Brent
chapters.fx: What to watch: the spread itself — if it narrows toward $5, the geopolitical premium is truly unwinding; if it stays wide, the market still prices Hormuz risk. For CAD, WTI is the number that moves the terms of trade; for JPY/EUR, Brent. Any fresh strike or shipping disruption re-prices Brent first and the spread blows wider within hours.

scenarios.base: Brent drifts $100–105 while the no-strikes pledge holds; CAD trades the jobs beat more than the oil tape.
scenarios.bull: A fresh escalation or Hormuz disruption: Brent spikes toward $110+, the spread blows past $15; CAD rips on WTI follow-through, JPY/EUR sag on import-cost fears.
scenarios.bear: Ceasefire chatter or OPEC+ supply signals: Brent breaks under $100, spread collapses toward $5; CAD gives back the jobs gains, importers breathe easier.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Gold holds ~$4,189 as the softer dollar and easing yields revive the bid — still ~21% below January's $5,318 peak.
chapters.meaning: What changed: gold firmed today alongside the dollar's slide, recovering as Treasury yields eased and the war premium leaked out of crude but lingered in haven demand. Thread: gold topped $5,318 in late January at the peak of the Iran escalation scare, then bled lower for months as the Fed's hawkish hold kept real yields elevated and the dollar ripped to 18-month highs. What it means: gold is trading as the anti-dollar right now, not the war hedge — it rises when the dollar softens and yields fall, which is exactly today's tape. For FX, firm gold is a soft headwind for USD and a quiet tell on risk appetite: when gold and equities rise together, the market is hedging the dollar, not fearing the world.
chapters.fx: What to watch: a break back above $4,300 would signal the haven bid is broadening beyond dollar-weakness — historically a USD-negative, CHF/JPY-positive setup. Conversely, a hot CPI next Wednesday that revives hike bets would likely knock gold back as real yields climb.

scenarios.base: Gold consolidates $4,100–4,300 into Wednesday's CPI; direction comes from the print, not the metal.
scenarios.bull: CPI undershoots and hike bets collapse — gold breaks $4,300 and the anti-dollar trade broadens.
scenarios.bear: Hot CPI revives the October hike; real yields jump and gold slides back toward $4,000.

headline: The dollar pauses as Trump takes an Iran strike off the table — the war premium leaks out, but the Fed's hawkish-hold thesis stands.
